target_customer: Construction and utility contractors, civil engineers, design firms and insurers exposed to utility strikes
problem: Contractors dig without accurate maps of buried utilities, causing dangerous strikes and costly delays.
business_model: Mapping services performed by autonomous rovers, sold to contractors per project
product_category: Underground utility mapping with ground penetrating radar robots and computer vision

founders.name: Maxwell Stone
education: University of Pennsylvania, MSE and BSE in Computer Science (per YC page)

founders.name: Wenson Tang
education: University of Pennsylvania, Computer Science and Consumer Psychology (per YC page)

competitors.name: Exodigo
competitors.what: AI and multi-sensor non-intrusive underground mapping

competitors.name: Subsite GeoRanger XR
competitors.what: GPR carts to find shallow and deep utilities

competitors.name: ULC Technologies AUSMOS
competitors.what: Robotic GPR system for utility damage prevention

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous rovers with ground penetrating radar need hardware, radar interpretation and centimeter-accurate 3D mapping; small teams have done early versions but accuracy in varied soils is hard.

defensibility.rationale: Better funded rivals exist and radar hardware is commercial. A growing map and labeled data set could compound, but is not proven.

market_need_then: Utility strikes cost the construction industry billions, and Exodigo's large Series B in July 2025 showed investor interest in subsurface mapping.

identity.logo: Wordmark only on a sparse landing page

brand_strength.rationale: Only a title and tagline on the site and no brand coverage found; the unusual spelling may cause misspellings.

outcome_analysis: The company is active in Summer 2026 with no exit and no verified funding beyond YC. It faces a large funded competitor in Exodigo and established GPR vendors, so its early rover fleet traction in Philadelphia and Texas needs to turn into repeat contractor demand.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked lists $355K total (March 2026) and Dealroom a $125k seed; neither has a primary source. A CB Insights snippet calls the founders UPenn dropouts, which conflicts with the YC page degrees; not used. Fleet in Philadelphia and Texas comes from that same snippet. No outcome news found. Completeness pass: Round recorded rests on VCBacked (seed, March 2026, $355K total there); amount left null because Dealroom shows a conflicting $125k seed.
